chunks: Behold, every follower has an Imam whom he follows and from the light of whose knowledge he takes illumination.
Behold, your Imam has contented himself with two shabby pieces of cloth from his worldly comforts, and two loaves for his meal.
Behold, you cannot do as I have done, but support me with piety, exertion, chastity, and uprightness.

By Allah, I have not treasured any gold from your world, nor amassed plentiful wealth from its spoils, nor collected for myself any clothes other than the two shabby sheets, nor gathered from its land any bundles, nor taken from it except as much as the food of an old donkey, and in my eyes it is weaker and more insignificant than a handful of dry grass.

key_terms.أَتَانٍ دَبِرَةٍ: An old donkey, used as a metaphor for insignificance
key_terms.إِمَاماً: Leader or guide whom followers emulate
key_terms.اجْتِهَادٍ: Exertion or striving in religious duties
key_terms.طِمْرَيْهِ: Two pieces of coarse or shabby cloth, symbolizing simplicity
key_terms.قُرْصَيْهِ: Two loaves of bread, symbolizing basic sustenance

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about his personal wealth and simplicity of life?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited as a cornerstone of Shia asceticism (Zuhd), emphasizes that the Imam’s authority is derived from spiritual light and knowledge rather than material accumulation, contrasting his voluntary poverty with the potential greed of other rulers. The vivid metaphor of his sustenance being 'like the food of an old donkey' underscores his complete detachment from worldly status, inviting the community to compensate for his lack of wealth through their own piety and diligence. This declaration serves as a theological and practical model for leadership, asserting that true authority requires no earthly treasury.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Remember that every follower has a leader whom he follows and from the effulgence of whose knowledge he takes light.
Realize that your Imam has contented himself with two shabby pieces of cloth out of the (comforts of the) world and two loaves for his meal.
Certainly, you cannot do so but at least support me in piety, exertion, chastity and uprightness,
because, by Allāh, I have not treasured any gold out of your world nor amassed plentiful wealth nor collected any clothes other than the two shabby sheets. ---
